c.tagline: Vietnam's beach-and-bridges city — My Khe sands, the Dragon Bridge, and a gateway to Hoi An.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis (Mai Linh, Vinasun) are reliable, but Grab and the electric Xanh SM are usually cheaper and remove any haggling over the fare.

emergency.note: 114 reaches the fire service. Operators may have limited English; hotel reception can help relay an emergency.

hood_landmark.Sơn Trà: Linh Ung Pagoda Son Tra Da Nang
hood_landmark.Thanh Khê: Da Nang city beach Nguyen Tat Thanh

avoid.reason: Motorbike bag- and phone-snatching occurs along the beach roads; keep phones away from the curb side.

hood_desc: The downtown core on the west bank of the Han River, home to the Dragon Bridge, Han Market, Da Nang Cathedral and the Cham Museum; the most convenient, walkable base for first-timers who want the city's sights, cafes and riverfront at their doorstep.

The beachside tourist quarter behind My Khe Beach, packed with Western and Vietnamese restaurants, bars, spas, dive shops and co-working cafes; the go-to area for nightlife, dining and digital nomads.

The peninsula and eastern riverbank district, running from the Han River Bridge up to the Son Tra headland with Linh Ung Pagoda and the Lady Buddha statue; a quieter, upscale mix of beach resorts, seafood spots and sea views.

The southern coastal district around the Marble Mountains and Non Nuoc Beach, lined with luxury beach resorts and the marble-carving village; suits travelers who want landmark sightseeing paired with a resort-style stay.

A local, residential district on the northern city-beach side near the railway station; less touristy and better value, good for travelers who want an everyday-Vietnam feel within a short ride of downtown.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not potable for visitors.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 6:00 PM; there is no late-night public transit, so Grab, Xanh SM and taxis cover the evenings.
transit.note: Da Nang has no metro or tram; a network of public city buses serves the main corridors, but most visitors get around by Grab, Xanh SM (electric taxis/bikes), taxis and rented motorbikes.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the conductor (around 5,000-20,000 VND depending on the route); there is no city-wide smartcard, and ride-hailing apps are paid in-app or in cash.

bus: Open-tour and sleeper buses to Hoi An, Hue, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City
train: Da Nang Railway Station (North-South Reunification line to Hue, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City)

transit.m: Grab or metered taxi to the city center (10-15 min)
Public city bus to downtown (limited routes, ~25 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service at tourist-facing restaurants and for spa or tour staff is appreciated.

food.name: Mi Quang
food.desc: Central Vietnam's defining noodle dish: wide turmeric noodles in just a splash of intense broth, with pork, shrimp, peanuts and a rice cracker.

places.name: Mi Quang 1A
places.note: Michelin-selected; glossy yellow noodles with pork, shrimp and chicken in one bowl.

places.name: Mi Quang Ba Mua
places.note: Polished, easy-to-find local chain if you would rather sit down than perch kerbside.

places.name: Mi Quang Hong Van
places.note: Bib Gourmand pick, distinctive for its orange-red shrimp broth and quail-egg topping.

food.name: Banh trang cuon thit heo
food.desc: Two-ended boiled pork belly rolled in rice paper with a fistful of herbs and green banana, dunked in fermented anchovy sauce.

places.name: Quan Tran
places.note: The name locals give first; several branches, all busy, all rolling to order.

places.name: Banh Trang Cuon Thit Heo Mau
places.note: Rival institution with thicker-cut pork and a punchier mam nem dipping sauce.

food.name: Bun cha ca
food.desc: Clear noodle soup built on fish bones and pumpkin, with springy fried and steamed fish cake, tomato and a fierce chilli-shrimp paste.

places.name: Bun Cha Ca 109
places.note: Open around the clock and packed at breakfast; the reference bowl in the city.

places.name: Bun Cha Ca Ba Phien
places.note: Family shop known for hand-pounded fish cake rather than factory-made.

food.name: Banh xeo and nem lui
food.desc: Small crisp shrimp-and-pork crepes eaten with lemongrass pork skewers, both wrapped in rice paper and dipped in thick peanut sauce.

places.name: Banh Xeo Ba Duong
places.note: Down a smoky alley off Hoang Dieu; the city's most famous banh xeo address.

places.name: Banh Xeo 76
places.area: Le Van Huu, Ngu Hanh Son
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand 2025 for shatteringly crisp crepes and charcoal nem lui.

food.name: Goi ca Nam O
food.desc: Raw herring cured in lime and rice wine, tossed with roasted rice powder, galangal and herbs. A Nam O fishing-village speciality.

places.name: Nam O village eateries
places.note: Cluster of family stalls in the village itself, where the dish was invented.

places.name: Goi Ca Nam O Thanh Huong
places.note: The best-known name in the village; order both the dry and the wet versions.

food.name: Grilled and steamed seafood
food.desc: Scallops with peanuts and spring onion, tamarind crab, garlic razor clams and salt-grilled squid, ordered by weight from the tank.

places.name: Be Man Seafood
places.note: Big, noisy, local-priced seafood house; point at the tanks and pick your cooking style.

places.name: My Khe beachfront strip
places.note: Row of open-air grills facing the sand, best around sunset.

food.name: Ca phe sua da and salt coffee
food.desc: Phin-dripped robusta over condensed milk and ice, plus central Vietnam's salted-cream coffee, a lightly savoury local twist.

places.name: 43 Factory Coffee Roaster
places.note: Serious in-house roastery bridging Vietnamese phin coffee and third-wave brewing.

places.name: Cong Caphe
places.note: Riverside branch of the retro chain; the coconut coffee is the crowd-pleaser.

food.name: Bia Larue
food.desc: Central Vietnam's own lager, brewed locally since French colonial days, poured over ice and drunk with grilled seafood.

places.name: My Khe beachfront strip
places.note: Iced Larue with a seafood grill and the sea a few metres away.

places.name: Son Tra Night Market
places.note: Beer and street snacks by the Dragon Bridge, cheapest after 8pm.

landmarks: Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son)
Five limestone-and-marble outcrops honeycombed with Buddhist cave sanctuaries, pagodas and stairways climbing to coastal panoramas south of the city.
Dragon Bridge (Cau Rong)
A 666-metre steel dragon spans the Han River and breathes real fire and water every weekend night, Da Nang's beloved modern icon.
My Khe Beach
A gorgeous 30-kilometre arc of soft white sand and rolling surf once dubbed China Beach, backed by seafood restaurants and beachfront resorts.
Lady Buddha and Linh Ung Pagoda
Vietnam's tallest Buddha statue, a 67-metre white Goddess of Mercy, gazes over the bay from the Son Tra Peninsula's flower-filled pagoda grounds.
Son Tra Peninsula (Monkey Mountain)
A jungle-clad nature reserve minutes from downtown, home to rare red-shanked douc langurs, hidden coves and sweeping city-and-sea viewpoints.
Museum of Cham Sculpture
The world's finest collection of Champa artefacts, hundreds of sandstone deities and dancing apsaras carved between the 5th and 15th centuries.
Han Market
Da Nang's classic riverside market piles high dried seafood, fabrics, spices and street snacks, the liveliest place to haggle like a local.
Da Nang Cathedral (Pink Church)
A candy-pink 1923 French Gothic church topped by a rooster weathervane, the city's prettiest colonial landmark and a favourite photo stop.
APEC Park
A riverside sculpture park beside the Han River shaped like a giant conical hat, filled with artworks gifted by Asia-Pacific nations and lit up at night.
Con Market (Cho Con)
Da Nang's largest traditional market, a sprawling maze of produce stalls, household goods and street-food vendors built on a sand dune in 1940.

train.note: Da Nang Railway Station sits on the North-South Reunification line, and there are no international rail services from anywhere in central Vietnam - the country's only cross-border train runs from Hanoi to Nanning. SE and TN trains run north to Hue in about 2.5 hours, one of Vietnam's most scenic rail stretches as the line clings to the coast over the Hai Van Pass, then on to Hanoi in roughly 16 to 17 hours, and south to Ho Chi Minh City in about 17 hours. Book on dsvn.vn or at the station; soft-sleeper berths on the overnight trains sell out around Tet and the summer holidays.

intl.to: Savannakhet, Pakse & Vientiane (Laos) - west through the Lao Bao border
intl.op: Vietnamese and Lao cross-border operators, tickets via VeXeRe

bus.note: Long-distance services use the Da Nang Central Bus Station a few kilometres out of town, served by city bus 2. Open-tour buses and shuttles run constantly to Hoi An (about 45 min) and to Hue (about 2.5 to 3 hr, though most use the tunnel rather than the Hai Van Pass), while sleeper coaches link Da Nang with Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City overnight. Cross-border coaches head west through the Lao Bao checkpoint to Savannakhet, Pakse and Vientiane in Laos; these are run by small Vietnamese and Lao companies rather than one carrier, so book at the station, through your accommodation or on the VeXeRe platform. Most nationalities can get a Lao visa on arrival at Lao Bao, but bring US dollars in cash and a passport photo.

ferry.note: Da Nang's port handles cargo and cruise ships rather than scheduled passenger ferries; the main on-water options for visitors are Han River dinner and sightseeing cruises.

half.name: Hoi An Ancient Town
half.blurb: A UNESCO-listed old trading port of lantern-lit streets, tailor shops and riverside cafes (~45 min).

half.name: Ba Na Hills & Golden Bridge
half.blurb: A mountaintop resort reached by a record-setting cable car, famous for the giant-hands Golden Bridge (~45 min).

half.name: Hai Van Pass
half.blurb: A dramatic coastal mountain pass with sweeping views over the bay, best by motorbike or car (~40 min).

full.name: My Son Sanctuary
full.blurb: A UNESCO complex of ruined Hindu brick towers built by the Cham civilization in a jungle valley (~1.5 hr).

full.name: Hue Imperial City
full.blurb: The former imperial capital, with its walled Citadel, royal tombs and Perfume River (~2.5 hr).

full.name: Bach Ma National Park
full.blurb: A cool highland park of waterfalls, trails and misty summit views between Da Nang and Hue (~1.5 hr).
